subject: Modeling missing values in sequential models

messages.author: a42d70b5905ad74a
messages.subject: Modeling missing values in sequential models
parts:
Hi!

I'm looking into handle missing values in a state space model by incorporating the missing values as parameters in the model. It is straight-forward in a model where there is no time structure as is expressed by the Stan manual for missing data. Is there any "obvious way" to handle missing data as parameters in this situation?

The simplest model can expressed like the one below. How do I handle missing values in y by incorporating them as parameters as has been shown in the Stan manual?

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real y[N];
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma_dynamic;
}

model {
  # Prior
  sigma_dynamic ~ gamma(1, 1);
  
  # Model/likelihood
  for(t in 2:(N - 1))
    y[t] ~ normal(y[t-1], sigma_dynamic);
}

generated quantities {
  real pred_y;
  pred_y = normal_rng(y[N-1], sigma_dynamic);
}

messages.author: 61924cbc2e733aae
messages.subject: Re: Modeling missing values in sequential models
parts:
Hi Måns,

Until someone post a less naive piece of code you could try something like this:

data {
  int<lower=1> N1;
  int<lower=1> N2;
  real yd[N1];
  int mask[N1+N2];
}

transformed data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  N = N1 + N2;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma_dynamic;
  real yp[N2];
}

model {
  real y[N];
  int c1;
  int c2;
  c1 = 1;
  c2 = 1;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    if (mask[n] == 0) {
      y[n] = yd[c1];
      c1 = c1 + 1;
    }
    else {
      y[n] = yp[c2];
      c2 = c2 + 1;
    }
  }
  sigma_dynamic ~ gamma(1, 1);
 
  for(t in 2:N)

y[t] ~ normal(y[t-1], sigma_dynamic);
}

Here yo define a mask with the distribution of datas and parameters of y.
You have to check that your mask comply with this rules: max(c1) == N1, max(c2) == N2. Also, you don't need y_pred, now it is another missing value that you have to put in the parameter yp.

I never try this code in particular, so maybe I'm wrong...

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Modeling missing values in sequential models
parts:
The idiomatic way to write that now with data slicing would be
to instead of storing the mask, just store the indexes of missing
items and indexes of observed items:


data {
int<lower = 0> N_obs;
int<lower = 0> N_mis;
int<lower = 0, upper = N_obs + N_mis> ii_obs[N_obs];
int<lower = 0, upper = N_obs + N_mis> ii_mis[N_mis];
real y_obs[N_obs];

parameters {
real y_mis[N_mis];
real y[N_obs + N_mis];
y[ii_obs] = y_obs;
y[ii_mis] = y_mis;

...

And then you're good to go (I didn't run this code, so someone
should double check it). The point is that ii_obs are the indexes
of the observed values and ii_mis are the indexes of the missing
values.

- Bob

I was just suggesting an alternative way to do the
same calculation. It won't be that much faster, just
cleaner.

If you're running into convergence issues, it may be because
the missing y are not well enough constrained by the model.
You have to make sure that the posteriors are proper.

- Bob

Hi!

Thanks to both of you! It now it seems to work out fine, the model is estimated in reasonable time and no convergence issues exists. I attach the final model (that is working) below if you want to include it in the chapter in missing data in the manual. I think it is clear how to solve these missing data situations. 

But the following message is now cast by RStan: 

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If it does, you need to include a target += statement with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    y[2:N] ~ normal(...)

In the model there are no transforms of the parameters (?), is this always thrown when we use a transform parameters {} step?

Stan model:

data {
  int<lower = 0> N_obs;
  int<lower = 0> N_mis;
  int<lower = 1, upper = N_obs + N_mis> ii_obs[N_obs];

  real y_obs[N_obs];
}

transformed data {
  int<lower = 0> N;
  N = N_obs + N_mis;
}

parameters {
  real y_mis[N_mis];
  real<lower=0> sigma_dynamic;

}

transformed parameters {
  real y[N_obs + N_mis];

y[ii_obs] = y_obs;
  y[ii_mis] = y_mis;
}

model {
  # Prior
  sigma_dynamic ~ gamma(1, 1);
  
  # Model/likelihood

y[2:N] ~ normal(y[1:(N - 1)], sigma_dynamic);
}
/Måns
